## How to report bugs and other problems
**To report a security issue (segfault, buffer overflow, infinite loop, arbitrary
code execution etc) please send an e-mail to security@tcpdump.org, do not use
the bug tracker!**

To report a non-security problem (failure to compile, incorrect output in the

first that it reproduces with the latest stable release of tcpdump and the latest

* steps to reproduce

Please note that if you know exactly how to solve the problem and the solution

Title: unsupported: do not print the packet bytes twice
Body:
Fixes #1387.

`unsupported_if_print()` has nothing to decode, so it prints the packet bytes itself. `pretty_print_packet()` prints them too when `-A`, `-x` or `-X` is given, so those options produced two dumps of the same bytes — with `-X`, two byte-identical hex and ASCII dumps back to back.

The implicit dump exists only so that an unsupported DLT shows *something*. It is now printed only when `pretty_print_packet()` will not print anything itself.

### Before / after

```
$ ./tcpdump -n -r tests/unsupported-link-type-160.pcap -X
reading from file tests/unsupported-link-type-160.pcap, link-type 160, snapshot length 102400
01:00:00.000000 UNSUPPORTED
	0x0000:  490c 6209 6923 34e8 efd3 a7bf 4ec0 fd3b  I.b.i#4.....N..;
	0x0010:  43e0 0b2b 2b2b 2b                        C..++++
-	0x0000:  490c 6209 6923 34e8 efd3 a7bf 4ec0 fd3b  I.b.i#4.....N..;
-	0x0010:  43e0 0b2b 2b2b 2b                        C..++++
```

Dumps printed per option, counted as occurrences of `0x0000:`:

| option | before | after | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *(none)* | 1 | 1 | unchanged — the implicit dump |
| `-X` | 2 | 1 | hex + ASCII |
| `-XX` | 2 | 1 | hex + ASCII, with link-layer header |
| `-x` | 2 | 1 | hex only, as `-x` means |
| `-A` | 1 | 0 | ASCII only, as `-A` means |

`-x` and `-A` were affected as well as `-X`, since the implicit dump is hex *and* ASCII regardless of which format was asked for. `-A` previously printed a full hex and ASCII dump in addition to the ASCII one, which is not what `-A` means.

I checked whether any sibling printer had the same problem before fixing this one — `print-unsupported.c` is the only `*_if_print()` that calls `hex_and_ascii_print()`, so the fix belongs here rather than in `pretty_print_packet()`.

### Tests

Added `unsupported-link-type-160-capX` (`-X`) and `unsupported-link-type-160-x` (`-x`), following the `capX` naming already used for `print-capX.out` so the files stay distinct on a case-insensitive filesystem. Expected output generated with `./update-test.sh`.

Both fail without the code change and pass with it:

```
with the fix reverted:    8 tests failed, 786 passed
with the fix:             6 tests failed, 788 passed
```

The 6 remaining failures are pre-existing on this machine and unrelated — `LINKTYPE_PKTAP`, `LINKTYPE_PKTAP-e` and the four 32-bit `time_t` tests. I verified they fail identically on unmodified `master`.

Built and tested on macOS 26.3, clang, with `.devel` for the extra warning options; no new warnings.
